question.text: In the convertible arb in Example 10.6: if the equity share price had FALLEN instead of risen, the chapter states the fund's gain would be approximately what %?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10.1.3 Example 10.6 commentary states: 'If the price of equity shares would have decreased, the Fund would not choose to convert the bonds into equity and square-off the short position in equity shares, with a net gain of 15%.' The Trap: A is arbitrary. B is borrow cost. D is the actual realised ROI under the rising-equity scenario. Cross-Exam Context: PDF Example 10.6 verbatim. XIX-C same. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 15% downside scenario assumes NO credit spread widening on the convertible — a key caveat. In a real credit crunch, the convertible bond loses value even if equity falls (floor erodes). Stress-test with both -20% equity AND +200 bps credit widening.
